title: AMD Helios MI400 System Architecture at Hot Chips 2026
gist: AMD detailed Helios, a 72-GPU rack combining EPYC Venice, Instinct MI455X, and Pensando Vulcano 800 AI NICs, claiming 2.9 exaflops, 31 TB of HBM4 and 1.7 PB/s of HBM4 bandwidth per rack. The strategic wedge is UALoE, a distributed shared-memory scale-up fabric running over open Ethernet and ESUN on often-Broadcom switches, deliberately positioned against proprietary interconnects.

themes.theme: Rack-scale as the new unit of competition

insights.claim: Each Helios rack holds 72 GPUs, 31 TB of HBM4, and 2.9 exaflops of claimed AI compute, with 1.7 PB/s of HBM4 bandwidth, 260 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth, and 43 TB/s of scale-out bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: These are the numbers to line up directly against NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 when evaluating who wins 2026-2027 AI rack deployments.
insights.quote: Each Helios rack holds 72 GPUs, 31 TB of HBM4, and 2.9 exaflops of claimed AI compute, with 1.7 PB/s of HBM4 bandwidth, 260 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth, and 43 TB/s of scale-out bandwidth.
insights.locator: Each Helios rack holds 72 GPUs

insights.claim: AMD argues AI infrastructure now has to be co-designed across CPUs, GPUs, software, networking, FPGAs, SoCs, and finished systems rather than assembled from separate parts.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Co-design as a requirement raises the barrier for component-only vendors and favors the two full-stack suppliers.
insights.locator: AMD opens by framing itself as a full-system company

insights.claim: Helios is built from three co-designed silicon blocks: a 96 core AMD EPYC Venice, an Instinct MI455X, and a Pensando Vulcano AI NIC.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD monetizes three sockets per node versus competitors selling one, improving revenue per rack even at similar GPU counts.
insights.quote: There is a 96 core AMD EPYC Venice, an Instinct MI455X and a Pensando Vulcano AI NIC.
insights.locator: Now AMD lays out the three co-designed silicon blocks

insights.claim: A 44OU ORW-HPR chassis holds 18 compute trays and six switch trays in the 72-GPU configuration, with blind-mate quick-disconnect liquid cooling, redundant power supplies, and a 50V DC LC busbar.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD's 50V DC busbar contrasts with the 800 VDC direction rivals are taking, a divergence with real data center facility implications.
insights.locator: AMD then shows how the Helios rack is physically constructed

insights.claim: AMD went from gluing four 8-core CCDs together in the 2017 EPYC to building rack-scale infrastructure in the span of nine years.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Track record argument for AMD's ability to execute against NVIDIA at system scale, relevant to multi-year supplier commitments.
insights.quote: It is quite remarkable that AMD has gone from “gluing” four 8-core CCDs together in the 2017 AMD EPYC to building rack-scale infrastructure in the span of 9 years.
insights.locator: Final Words

themes.theme: UALoE: open fabric as the strategic wedge

insights.claim: AMD stresses that UALoE is built on open Ethernet and ESUN standards and on often-Broadcom switches rather than a closed fabric, a deliberate contrast to proprietary scale-up interconnects from rivals.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Open scale-up fabric is AMD's main non-price lever against NVLink lock-in, and it pulls merchant switch silicon vendors into the AI rack value chain.
insights.quote: AMD stresses that UALoE is built on open Ethernet and ESUN standards, and on (often) Broadcom switches, rather than on a closed fabric.
insights.locator: AMD stresses that UALoE is built on open Ethernet

insights.claim: UALoE implements a distributed shared memory model where importer and exporter applications map buffers in GPU HBM through mmap, so remote and local nodes exchange data over a shared memory fabric with DMA doing the movement.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A load/store shared-memory programming model across a rack is what makes 72 GPUs usable as one engine, the capability customers actually pay for.
insights.locator: Now AMD is showing the distributed shared memory model

insights.claim: Each MI455X integrates 18x 800 Gbps UALoE adapters, and the fabric uses a lightweight reliable protocol with dynamic packet packing to trade off bandwidth and latency.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Integrating 800G adapters onto the GPU itself removes discrete scale-up NICs, changing the component bill for AI racks.
insights.quote: Each MI455X integrates 18x 800 Gbps UALoE adapters
insights.locator: This figure digs into the transport itself

insights.claim: Topology-aware DMA engines offload data movement from the WGPs and run in parallel with compute, using a frontend-backend architecture that dynamically distributes load and keeps backends adjacent to the UALoE links.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Moving data movement off compute units is the practical mechanism for keeping GPU utilization high at rack scale.
insights.locator: UALoE extends that load/store view

insights.claim: AMD notes the Helios scale-up hop is currently electrical and approaching an optical transition, with the already-announced next generation starting to move to optical.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A concrete near-term catalyst for co-packaged and pluggable optics demand inside the rack, not just between racks.
insights.quote: AMD notes the scale-up hop is currently electrical and approaching an optical transition. They said something just now on stage that the already announced next-gen will start to transition to optical as well.
insights.locator: Next comes the scale-up pod

insights.claim: The Helios switch tray uses two 512-port 200G UALoE switch ASICs delivering 10.8 TB/s/dir with 72 active links per switch, in a roughly 7kW liquid-cooled tray managed by a Ryzen-based BMC.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A 7kW switch tray shows networking is now a meaningful share of rack power, a cost line often ignored in GPU-centric TCO models.
insights.locator: Next comes the switch tray

insights.claim: On a whole switch tray loss, DMA rebalances over the five remaining trays of six and WGP references rebalance under software control, keeping the fabric alive as a full tray disappears.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Graceful degradation on tray loss is what turns a 72-GPU rack from a single point of failure into a production asset.
insights.locator: What about with a whole switch tray loss?

insights.claim: Virtual pods let operators combine a subset of nodes into an isolated VPod so node-level failures remain contained to the affected VPod instead of taking down the whole rack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Partitioning is the feature that makes rack-scale systems rentable to multiple tenants, expanding the buyer set beyond single-tenant labs.
insights.locator: Virtual pods give operators flexible partitioning

insights.claim: AMD Fabric Manager runs as a three-node cluster on the scale-up switches, surviving a single failure and dropping to read-only on a double failure, and manages the scale-up network and compute without depending on the host stack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A host-independent control plane is an operational differentiator that reduces blast radius during host software failures.
insights.locator: Above that hardware, AMD Fabric Manager (AFM)

insights.claim: AMD's rack-scale confidential computing spans EPYC, MI455X, and the AI NIC with secure boot, a DICE-based root of trust, universal link encryption with fast key rotation, and SEV-SNP external memory encryption.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Confidential computing parity is a prerequisite for regulated and sovereign AI deployments, a fast-growing segment of demand.
insights.locator: AMD is now laying out rack-scale confidential computing

insights.claim: A footnote cautions that a malicious hypervisor can undermine some integrity guarantees on the current MI455X, though data and model confidentiality still hold.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A disclosed integrity gap in the current generation is exactly the detail security-sensitive buyers will use to defer purchases to the next revision.
insights.quote: A footnote cautions that a malicious hypervisor can undermine some integrity guarantees on the current MI455X, though data and model confidentiality still hold.
insights.locator: AMD is now laying out rack-scale confidential computing

insights.claim: The Vulcano 800 is a P4-based design with 192 MPUs, P4DMA engines for RDMA and storage, PCIe Gen6 x16 and UAL128 host interfaces, and a single 800G network port.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A P4 pipeline rather than an Arm core farm is a distinct DPU architecture bet with different power and programmability trade-offs.
insights.locator: Here is the Vulcano 800 block diagram

insights.claim: AMD believes P4 is the way to go over a sea of Arm cores for the programmable part of an AI NIC.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Directly contradicts the Arm-core DPU approach used by rivals, a live architectural argument in the DPU market.
insights.quote: I asked Soni at AAI, and AMD thinks P4 is the way to go over a sea of Arm cores for the programmable part.
insights.locator: Here is the Vulcano 800 block diagram

insights.claim: The Vulcano P4 engine can carry and interpret custom congestion-control signals and maintain state for newer schemes such as MRC and UEC's framework while still supporting classic DCQCN.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Programmable congestion control future-proofs the NIC against unsettled AI networking standards, reducing obsolescence risk for buyers.
insights.locator: Congestion control gets the same programmability treatment

insights.claim: In an all-reduce comparison, MRC offers a throughput advantage with a single queue pair versus RoCEv2's escalating QP counts, with AMD crediting packet spray and selective acknowledgment for drop convergence at the edge on larger messages.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: If single-QP MRC really beats multi-QP RoCEv2, RDMA fabric tuning burden drops materially, lowering operational cost of large clusters.
insights.locator: This figure compares MRC against RoCEv2

insights.claim: An 800G Vulcano port can present as 1x800G, 2x400G, 4x200G, or 8x100G for message sizes of 64 KB or larger.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Lane flexibility lets one NIC SKU serve multiple network generations, easing deployment into mixed existing fabrics.
insights.locator: Here AMD shows Vulcano MRC performance

insights.claim: Each Helios compute tray packs four Instinct MI455X modules with a single Venice SP7 CPU host, giving each GPU node 1.8 TB/s/dir of UALoE scale-up bandwidth across 12 3x2 links plus coherent Infinity Fabric at 128 GB/s/dir to the CPU.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A 4:1 GPU-to-CPU ratio sets how many EPYC sockets ship per AI rack, a direct input to AMD server CPU volume forecasts.
insights.locator: Inside each compute tray

insights.claim: Each MI455X gets 1.8 TB/s/dir across 72 IFoE links at 200G in the scale-up pod, while 800G NICs hang scale-out Ethernet off the same pod with up to 2.4 Tb/s/dir per GPU.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Per-GPU scale-out bandwidth of 2.4 Tb/s drives optics and switch port demand per accelerator shipped.
insights.locator: Next comes the scale-up pod

insights.claim: The switched scale-up topology gives every GPU shared load/store access across the entire 72-GPU pod rather than within a local rack segment.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Full-pod load/store access is the technical claim that lets AMD say 72 GPUs act as one engine, matching NVIDIA's NVL72 pitch.
insights.locator: Pulling back, AMD shows the full 72-GPU Helios pod

insights.claim: NVIDIA will still sell a lot of Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, but having a second GPU vendor operating at rack scale is a meaningful market change.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Frames Helios as a credible second source rather than a share-taker, which matters more for NVIDIA pricing power than for unit share.
insights.quote: NVIDIA is still going to sell a lot of Vera Rubin NVL72 racks, but it is always good to have a second GPU vendor operating at this scale.
insights.locator: Final Words
